name: Cosmic CRF Ltd
tagline: BSE-SME cold-rolled-form / railway-wagon-component maker with an integrated-wagon roll-up ambition - the Supreme Court has now vacated the NCLAT Section 29A ineligibility finding, materially lifting the biggest overhang
business_overview: Manufacturer of cold-rolled formed sections and railway wagon components for Indian Railways and PSUs, pursuing an 'integrated wagon manufacturer' roll-up (Amzen bid); BSE-SME listed.
fundamentals_table: Revenue ~Rs 717-723 Cr vs ~Rs 402 Cr FY25 (+~78-80%); PAT ~Rs 51 Cr vs ~Rs 29-31 Cr (+~74%); OPM ~11% (flat)
~133,600 MTPA; installed capacity +~94% YoY; order book ~Rs 760 Cr; springs volume target 10-12k MT FY27, 22-23k MT FY28
FY26 CFO +Rs 24 Cr (FY25 -Rs 73 Cr) - turned positive; FY26 FCF -Rs 109 Cr on Rs 145 Cr capex; borrowings Rs 133 Cr (up from Rs 78 Cr), +Rs 200 Cr loan planned for the Amzen integration
Supreme Court (14-May-2026, Civil Appeals 4266-4267/2026) allowed Cosmic's appeals, upheld Section 29A eligibility, set aside NCLAT orders; reinstated as H1 bidder for the Amzen wagon plant
fundamentals_narrative: FY26 was a strong operating year - revenue nearly doubled to ~Rs 717-723 Cr, PAT +~74% to ~Rs 51 Cr, installed capacity +~94% - though margins stayed thin (OPM ~11%) and returns are still sub-bar (ROCE ~13.6%, ROE ~11.9%). Two things have improved since the prior read: (1) the Supreme Court (14-May-2026) allowed Cosmic's appeals, held it was not disqualified under Section 29A, set aside the NCLAT ineligibility orders and reinstated it as H1 bidder for the Amzen integrated-wagon plant - removing the single largest bear point; (2) FY26 operating cash flow turned positive (+Rs 24 Cr vs -Rs 73 Cr in FY25). But free cash flow is deeply negative (-Rs 109 Cr on Rs 145 Cr capex), borrowings are rising (Rs 133 Cr, with a further Rs 200 Cr loan planned for Amzen), and the third-party forgery allegation against MD Aditya Vikram Birla over the Raft Cosmic EV JV share transfer (forged SH-4, per Raft Motors' founder) is still unresolved. The FY26 springs/fabricated-steel line did ~Rs 67 Cr revenue at just ~Rs 1.5 Cr margin because RDSO licensing was delayed - the FY27 margin story hinges on those licences coming through.
sentiment_summary: No new forum activity since the prior read (thread stable, highest #84). The Supreme Court outcome is confirmed via public sources / the Q4 concall ('legal victory'), not via new thread posts.

verdict_headline: Re-verification: the Supreme Court has cleared the Section 29A ineligibility finding and FY26 growth is strong - conviction raised to Low-Medium and the HIGH CAUTION tier removed, with cash-flow quality and the EV-JV allegations still to monitor
verdict_reasoning: Re-verification stock (Sovrenn lead). The H2 FY26 growth datapoint is verified, and separately the Supreme Court has set aside the NCLAT Section 29A orders and upheld Cosmic's eligibility - the primary driver of the earlier HIGH CAUTION tier is gone.

With the apex-court cloud lifted, ~90% FY26 volume growth, a railway-capex upcycle and a small Rs 795 Cr base, conviction moves up one notch to Low-Medium; the red_flag_tier is cleared to null, with the Raft Cosmic EV-JV allegations and the historically weak cash flow named as the remaining watch items.

four_box score is 2.5 (tailwind yes / tam-moat-valuation weak). Written exception per the decision table: FY26 revenue nearly doubled, capacity is up ~94% and the order book (Rs 760 Cr) is ~1x revenue - growth is un-ignorable (phreak's carve-out) - so thesis_fit stays 10x-in-2-3-years with conviction capped at Medium; it actually sits at Low-Medium given -Rs 109 Cr FCF, rising debt into the Amzen roll-up, sub-15% ROCE, an RDSO-dependent forward margin and the unresolved forgery allegation against the MD.

four_box.note: Railway-capex upcycle for wagons/rolling-stock is a real structural tailwind; small base (~Rs795cr) + roll-up optionality (Amzen/integrated wagon plant) is unproven execution — tam weak; no distinct moat vs peers (Titagarh, Jupiter Wagons) — weak; no valuation data, thin ~10% OPM and unconfirmed FY26 cash quality — weak. Supreme Court vacating the NCLAT Section 29A ineligibility is a major cleared overhang; Raft Cosmic EV-JV forgery allegations remain unresolved.
